corpus.title: xochitl · flower
corpus.summary: Flower; this record uses Molina's botanical sense. The same headword can also occur as a personal name or calendar sign.
corpus.citation: Molina, Vocabulario (1571), part 2, f. 160r, col. 2. Online Nahuatl Dictionary, Stephanie Wood, ed., University of Oregon.

corpus.title: cuahuitl · tree / wood
corpus.summary: Molina records quauitl for a tree, timber, or a stick. This record selects the tree sense; other contexts require disambiguation.
corpus.citation: Molina (1571), part 2, f. 88r, col. 1. Online Nahuatl Dictionary, Stephanie Wood, ed., University of Oregon.

corpus.title: xochicuahuitl · flowering tree
corpus.summary: A flowering tree. The entry points to a description and illustration in the Florentine Codex, Book 11, f. 187v.
corpus.citation: Florentine Codex (1577), Book 11, f. 187v, referenced by the Online Nahuatl Dictionary, Stephanie Wood, ed., University of Oregon.
corpus.caveat: Botanical identifications differ across sources. Do not treat liquidambar, black sage, and any flowering tree as interchangeable species. Modern ceremonial examples on the dictionary page are excluded.

corpus.title: atl · water
corpus.summary: Water is the selected sense. Molina also lists other senses; a modern sentence must be interpreted in context.
corpus.citation: Molina (1571), part 2, f. 8r; Carochi (1645), Lockhart edition (2001), p. 498. Online Nahuatl Dictionary, Stephanie Wood, ed., University of Oregon.

corpus.title: calli · house
corpus.summary: A house or building. Lockhart also gives nominal-predicate readings: it is a house, or they are houses. Context determines the reading.
corpus.citation: Lockhart, Nahuatl as Written (2001), p. 212. Online Nahuatl Dictionary, Stephanie Wood, ed., University of Oregon.
corpus.period: Scholarly analysis of older written Nahuatl

corpus.title: tonatiuh · sun
corpus.summary: The sun, as recorded by Molina. Other attestations may concern a day or a named divine force; those senses are not automatically implied.
corpus.citation: Molina (1571), part 2, f. 149v, col. 1. Online Nahuatl Dictionary, Stephanie Wood, ed., University of Oregon.

corpus.title: metztli · moon
corpus.summary: Moon or month. Vowel length distinguishes this from the word for leg in scholarly analysis; unmarked historical spelling can obscure that distinction.
corpus.citation: Molina (1571), part 2, f. 55v, col. 1; Karttunen (1992), p. 144. Online Nahuatl Dictionary, Stephanie Wood, ed., University of Oregon.

corpus.title: itta · to see
corpus.summary: To see or inspect. The transitive form needs appropriate subject and object marking. Modern Huastecan examples elsewhere on the source page are excluded.
corpus.citation: Molina (1571), part 2, f. 43r, col. 2; Lockhart (2001), p. 221. Online Nahuatl Dictionary, Stephanie Wood, ed., University of Oregon.

corpus.title: ihuan · and / with
corpus.summary: Molina records iuan as a conjunction meaning and or also. The normalized headword is ihuan. This record excludes modern shortened forms.
corpus.citation: Molina (1571), part 2, f. 43v, col. 1. Online Nahuatl Dictionary, Stephanie Wood, ed., University of Oregon.

corpus.title: niquitta · first-person transitive form
corpus.summary: Molina lists itta with niqu.; Lockhart also records (i)tta, niqu. This supports niquitta for I see it. Combining that form with a new noun phrase is an application, not a quotation of a historical sentence.
corpus.citation: Molina (1571), part 2, f. 43r, col. 2; Lockhart, Nahuatl as Written (2001), p. 221. Online Nahuatl Dictionary, Stephanie Wood, ed., University of Oregon.
corpus.caveat: Only the first-person singular subject and a singular third-person object are covered by the built-in composition rule.

corpus.title: Water as the heart of the sky
corpus.summary: An attested comparison involving water and the sky, recorded in Mexico City around 1582. Transcription and Spanish translation are accessed through the dictionary, not independently checked against the manuscript.
corpus.quote: in atl ca yuhquima yollo yn ilhuicatl
corpus.translation: El agua es como el corazón del cielo.
corpus.citation: Anales de Juan Bautista, ca. 1582; Luis Reyes García edition (2001), pp. 170–171, cited in the Online Nahuatl Dictionary, Stephanie Wood, ed., University of Oregon.

corpus.title: The disappearing moon
corpus.summary: A passage in Book 7 describes the moon's disappearance using the expression below. The English gloss here is a short explanatory rendering, not a claim about astronomical causation.
corpus.citation: Florentine Codex, Book 7; Anderson and Dibble edition (1961), p. 3, quoted in the Online Nahuatl Dictionary, Stephanie Wood, ed., University of Oregon.

corpus.title: Florentine Codex · Book 11, f. 187v
corpus.summary: The dictionary identifies a flowering-tree description and image at this manuscript location. This is a contextual manuscript pointer, not a sentence-level parallel translation.
corpus.citation: Florentine Codex (1577), Book 11, f. 187v. Digital edition: Getty Research Institute (2023). Locator documented in the Oregon xochicuahuitl entry.
corpus.caveat: The locator is corroborated through the dictionary. Direct manuscript text was not independently transcribed for this corpus.

corpus.title: Flower element · Codex Mendoza 10r
corpus.summary: Flower element extracted from the place-name compound Xochiacan. Its use here is a related historical visual, not a complete glyph translation of a new sentence.
corpus.citation: Codex Mendoza, f. 10r. Visual Lexicon of Aztec Hieroglyphs, Stephanie Wood, ed.

corpus.title: Water element · Codex Mendoza 51r
corpus.summary: Water element extracted from the place-name compound Ayotochco. The original name and manuscript context remain essential to its interpretation.
corpus.citation: Codex Mendoza, f. 51r. Visual Lexicon of Aztec Hieroglyphs, Stephanie Wood, ed.
corpus.rights: Bodleian Libraries, University of Oxford, MS. Arch. Selden. A. 1. Via Visual Lexicon of Aztec Hieroglyphs, Stephanie Wood, ed. CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 UK.

corpus.title: House element · Codex Mendoza 13r
corpus.summary: Building element extracted from the place-name compound Apancalecan. The entrance faces left in this particular example.
corpus.citation: Codex Mendoza, f. 13r. Visual Lexicon of Aztec Hieroglyphs, Stephanie Wood, ed.
corpus.rights: Bodleian Libraries, University of Oxford, MS. Arch. Selden. A. 1. Via Visual Lexicon of Aztec Hieroglyphs, Stephanie Wood, ed. CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 UK.

corpus.title: Flowering tree · Codex Mendoza 50r
corpus.summary: Tree element extracted from Xochicuauhtitlan, interpreted in the lexicon as Near the Liquidambar Trees. This place-name reading does not establish a universal botanical identification.
corpus.citation: Codex Mendoza, f. 50r. Visual Lexicon of Aztec Hieroglyphs, Stephanie Wood, ed.
